newsitem.title: USA: NHL-BRUINS SCORE TWICE IN LAST 1:17 TP BEAT FLYERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-BRUINS SCORE TWICE IN LAST 1:17 TP BEAT FLYERS.

text.p: Bob Beers and Ray Bourque scored 56 seconds apart in the final 1:17 of regulation as the lowly Boston Bruins overcame a hat trick by Trent Klatt to rally for a 5-5 tie with the Philadelphia Flyers Saturday.
After the game, the Bruins traded centre Adam Oates, right wing Rick Tocchet and goaltender Bill Ranford to the Washington Capitals for goalie Jim Carey and centres Anson Carter and Jason Allison.
Beers took a pass from Oates at the left point and one-timed a slap shot that beat Ron Hextall between the pads for his second goal of the season.

Oates, who led the Bruins in scoring five of his seasons with the team, also set up Bourque's tying goal. He threaded a pass from behind the net through several Flyers to the top of the slot. Bourque spun and fired a no-look shot that deflected off two defenders and over Hextall's left shoulder.
"All I know on Bourque's goal is he spun around, took a shot, it hit my stick. I saw it for an instant, but then lost it," said Hextall. "The fourth goal, I never saw."
Landon Wilson, Don Sweeney and Sheldon Kennedy also scored for Boston, which has gone 1-0-2 in its last three games to escape the Eastern Conference cellar.
Klatt got his first career hat trick for the Flyers, who are 6-1-2 in their last nine games and lead the East with 82 points.

"It's great when you can score three goals, but when the team doesn't win it takes a lot away from that," Klatt said. "Unfortunately, when you have a two-goal lead with two minutes to go, you shouldn't lose leads like that."

In Colorado, Adam Deadmarsh beat Jeff Hackett on a penalty shot to break a scoreless tie with 9:16 remaining in the game and Claude Lemieux added an insurance marker three minutes later as the Avalanche broke their two-game losing streak, 2-1 over the Chicago Blackhawks.

The Avalanche have not lost three straight games all season, but that streak appeared in jeopardy midway through the third period, when the Blackhawks had a power play. But Deadmarsh got a pass in the centre circle and had a clean breakaway when he was tripped from behind by Chris Chelios.
"I just dove to get him and I tripped him," Chelios admitted.
On the penalty shot, Deadmarsh deked and lifted a backhand shot low to Hackett's stick side and into the net for his team-best 25th goal of the season.

In Detroit, Chris Osgood moved into a tie for the league lead with his sixth shutout and Darren McCarty and Brendan Shanahan each had a goal and assist, leading the Red Wings to a 3-0 victory over the punchless New York Rangers.
Osgood turned aside 21 shots against a Rangers team lacking injured centres Mark Messier and Sergei Nemchinov.
The Red Wings stretched their unbeaten streak to seven games (5-0-2), equalling a season high.
In New Jersey, John MacLean had two goals and an assist as the Devils extended their franchise-record home unbeaten streak to 12 games, beating the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-3.
MacLean, whose bid for a hat trick on a partial breakaway was stopped by Ken Wregget, has 21 goals this season and has scored in consecutive games since the birth of his first child Thursday.
Doug Gilmour scored a goal for the third time in as many games since being traded from Toronto and added an assist to give him seven points as a Devil, helping New Jersey win its third straight.

In Ottawa, Donald Audette scored twice and Dominik Hasek posted his league-leading 32nd win as the Buffalo Sabres bounced back from their first loss in more than a month by shutting down the Senators 3-1.
Mike Peca had the other goal for the Sabres, whose 12-game unbeaten streak was snapped Thursday at New Jersey.
The Senators, 1-3-1 in their last five games, remained two points out of the final Eastern Conference playoff berth.

In Vancouver, Stephane Fiset made 35 saves to notch his fourth shutout of the season and second straight against the Canucks as the Los Angeles Kings extended their season-high winning streak to five games with a 3-0 victory.
Ray Ferraro, Brad Smyth and Jeff Shevalier scored for the Kings, who have won five straight for the first time since 1992. The Canucks have lost four of their last five games.
In Calgary, Jarome Iginla recorded his first career two-goal game and fellow rookie Dwayne Roloson made 32 saves as the Flames won their third win in four games, 4-1 over the Dallas Stars.
Iginla leads all rookies with 45 points.
Darryl Sydor scored the lone goal for the Stars, who had their four-game winning streak snapped and lost for just the second time in their last eight outings.
In Edmonton, former Oiler Scott Thornton scored his second goal of the game at 7:12 of the third period to lift the Montreal Canadiens to a 5-4 victory.
Valeri Bure had a goal and two assists for the Canadiens,
In Tampa, Rick Tabaracci stopped 24 shots for his third shutout of the season and Chris Gratton and Dino Ciccarelli scored as the Lightning beat the Florida Panthers 2-0.
Tampa Bay won for the fifth time in six games.
In Toronto, Tie Domi scored with 5:18 remaining to lift the Maple Leafs to a 3-2 victory over the San Jose Sharks in a matchup of the worst teams in the Western Conference.
